haiku-low.q1: Same response: 401 page "Invalid email or password". Both insert a login_failures row.
haiku-low.q2: The lock check runs first. It gets 429 "Too many attempts, try later". No password check runs and no failure is recorded.
haiku-low.q3: The session named by the incoming cookie is deleted, even if it belongs to another user. A new random ID is issued.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random 32-byte base64url session ID with no user data. It has the HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax flags. The document does not otherwise say what scripts can read.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours from creation. created_at never changes, so continuous use does not extend it. The 30-minute idle rule is not triggered while in use.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the row if it exists, clears the cookie, and redirects with 302 to /login.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session if any, then the browser gets a cookie clear and 302 to /login. If already gone, nothing is deleted and the same response is sent.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, shared by both app instances. Each instance loads the session by sid from that database. Redis is not used.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with lowercase email and failed_at. Failures with failed_at in the last 10 minutes count toward the 5-failure threshold.
haiku-low.q10: It checks now minus last_seen_at (over 30 min) and now minus created_at (over 12 h). If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 page reading "Something went wrong, try again". No session is issued.
haiku-low.q12: Each instance's hourly idempotent cleanup delete removes expired sessions, failures older than 10 minutes, and passed locks.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get a 401 login page saying "Invalid email or password" (a dummy bcrypt hash is run for unknown emails, and a failure row is recorded either way).
sonnet.q2: Once a lock exists for that email (locked_until > now), it gets a 429 login page "Too many attempts, try later". The password is not checked and no failure is recorded.
sonnet.q3: On successful login, the session named by the incoming cookie is deleted (even if it belongs to another user), and a new session with a new random ID is inserted and issued.
sonnet.q4: Only the sid, a random 32-byte ID (base64url) with no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it (also Secure, SameSite=Lax).
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after created_at, because created_at never changes. The 30-minute idle limit keeps being reset by activity.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if it exists, clears the cookie, and responds with a 302 redirect to /login.
sonnet.q7: It deletes the session row if any, then clears the cookie and returns a 302 to /login. If the session is already gone, nothing is deleted ("if any") and the same clear-cookie and redirect happen.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, keyed by sid. Both app instances share Postgres, so whichever instance gets the request looks up the sid from the cookie in the database.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email (lowercase) and failed_at. The server counts rows for that email with failed_at within the last 10 minutes (5 or more triggers a lock).
sonnet.q10: It compares now against last_seen_at (more than 30 min is expired) and against created_at (more than 12 h is expired). When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now.
sonnet.q11: A 503 page "Something went wrong, try again". No session is issued.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup, run by each instance as an idempotent delete, removes expired sessions.
